name: Martin McGuinness
role: Irish republican leader, former IRA commander and Northern Ireland deputy First Minister (2007–2017)
summary: McGuinness pursued Irish reunification and moved from the IRA campaign to negotiated peace and power-sharing. His later programme defended welfare and universal healthcare, European integration, Irish-language rights and equal marriage, while retaining restrictions on abortion.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2013 speech explicitly supported free universal healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He advocated a living wage so low-paid workers would not depend on state supplements; this supports higher wage floors without specifying a statutory increase.

unions-good.rationale: He praised trade unions for contributing to measures addressing the economic downturn.

cut-welfare.rationale: He opposed welfare retrenchment targeting vulnerable people and promised to block the bedroom tax.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He personally promised new legislation for equal marriage and rejected treating LGBT people as second-class citizens.

abortion-legal.rationale: He opposed abortion as birth control and later still rejected abortion on demand, while supporting exceptions including fatal fetal abnormality.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He defended Irish-language and cultural initiatives against political opposition.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He called for profound political and economic changes, a transition from fossil fuels to renewables and rainforest protection.

revolution-justified.rationale: He justified earlier armed resistance as a popular response to state repression and later declined to apologise for fighting British soldiers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He defended public capital spending specifically to stimulate construction and the economy.

right-to-secede.rationale: His proposed border poll would allow Northern Ireland to leave the United Kingdom and unite with Ireland; it does not establish an unlimited right for every region.

political-violence-never.rationale: Even in 2015 he defended having fought British troops, while advocating peace and opposing renewed violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: He opposed using religious authority to dictate government policy in a society of different faiths.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He rejected the argument that government should uphold scriptural morality, asking which religion’s God would govern.

national-self-determination.rationale: His mature goal remained an independent all-Ireland republic; the evidence specifically concerns Irish self-determination.

class-collaboration.rationale: He argued that economic recovery and protecting jobs required partnership, while praising union involvement in a cross-sector economic forum.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His resignation letter demanded equality and respect for everyone, explicitly criticising prejudice against women, LGBT people and ethnic minorities.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He challenged Brexit imposed against Northern Ireland’s vote and demanded elections so people could judge the Executive crisis.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He prioritised protecting frontline services and directing public spending toward those most in need.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He defended continued EU membership and a united Ireland within the European Union after the Brexit vote.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: His retirement statement reaffirmed his personal aim of ending the British link and uniting the island politically.

minority-language-support.rationale: He backed the Liofa Irish-language initiative and condemned attacks on people using Irish.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He urged cancellation of debts owed by poor Asian countries after the tsunami.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He offered dialogue to republicans opposing his strategy and to the Orange Order, keeping his office open to all sections.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He called inclusion and power-sharing foundational and rejected a return to rule by one community.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: In 2015 he explicitly opposed armed gangs and all paramilitary organisations as threats to the democratic settlement.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He called for a border referendum allowing voters to choose Irish reunification after a British vote to leave the EU.

notes: Later peacebuilding did not amount to an absolute repudiation of earlier armed resistance. Specific disputed allegations about IRA operations are not treated as established personal policy. Exceptional abortion access is distinguished from general legalisation; no positions are inferred from Sinn Féin membership. A 2015 BBC report is cited through an opened reproduction, excluding its host’s appended commentary. Student-fee protection does not establish free university tuition. All unanswered statements were reviewed against the gathered record.
